# Install Vault Client

Download [Vault Client](/vault/docs/client) from IBM Passport Advantage Online
or the IBM Entitled Registry, and confirm that it runs.

@include 'alerts/enterprise-only.mdx'

## Before you start

- **You must have a Vault Enterprise license**. Any Vault Enterprise customer
  can get access to IBM Passport Advantage Online and the IBM Entitled
  Registry. To sign in or request access, refer to
  [Passport Advantage Online for Customers][ibm-passport-advantage].

- **Check your Vault server version**. Vault Client 2.x works with Vault
  Enterprise deployments running v2.x or later and HCP Vault Dedicated.

- **Choose a binary or a container image**. IBM Passport Advantage Online
  provides binaries for Linux, AIX, and Windows, and container image archives
  for Linux. The IBM Entitled Registry provides container images for Linux.

## Step 1: Download Vault Client

<Tabs>

<Tab heading="Binary" group="binary">

1. Sign in to
   [IBM Passport Advantage Online][ibm-passport-advantage].

1. Download the Vault Client archive for your platform:

   Platform        | Archive
   --------------- | -------------------------------------
   Linux (amd64)   | `vault_<version>.cl_linux_amd64.zip`
   Linux (arm64)   | `vault_<version>.cl_linux_arm64.zip`
   Linux (ppc64le) | `vault_<version>.cl_linux_ppc64le.zip`
   Linux (s390x)   | `vault_<version>.cl_linux_s390x.zip`
   AIX (ppc64)     | `vault_<version>.cl_aix_ppc64.zip`
   Windows (386)   | `vault_<version>.cl_windows_386.zip`
   Windows (amd64) | `vault_<version>.cl_windows_amd64.zip`

1. Unzip the archive. The archive contains the `vault-client` binary, or
   `vault-client.exe` on Windows.

1. Move the binary to a directory in your system `PATH`. For example, on Linux:

   ```shell-session
   $ sudo mv vault-client /usr/bin/
   ```

</Tab>

<Tab heading="Image archive" group="image-archive">

1. Sign in to
   [IBM Passport Advantage Online][ibm-passport-advantage].

1. Download the Vault Client image archive for your architecture:

   Architecture | Archive
   ------------ | -----------------------------------
   amd64        | `vault_linux_amd64_<version>.cl.tar`
   arm64        | `vault_linux_arm64_<version>.cl.tar`
   ppc64le      | `vault_linux_ppc64le_<version>.cl.tar`
   s390x        | `vault_linux_s390x_<version>.cl.tar`

1. Load the image archive. For example:

   ```shell-session
   $ docker load --input vault_linux_amd64_2.2.2.cl.tar
   ```

You can find the loaded image with the tag `hashicorp/vault-enterprise:<version>-ent.client`.

</Tab>

<Tab heading="IBM Entitled Registry" group="ier">

1. Get your IBM entitlement key:

   1. Sign in to the
      [IBM Container Library](https://myibm.ibm.com/products-services/containerlibrary)
      with a user ID that has permission to download entitled software for
      your company.
   1. If you do not see your current entitlement key displayed, select **Get entitlement key**.
   1. Under **Access your container software**, click **Copy key**, and store
      the key in a safe location.
   1. Optional: Select **View library** to confirm that your Vault entitlement
      is listed.

1. Sign in to the IBM Entitled Registry with the username `cp` and your
   entitlement key as the password:

   ```shell-session
   $ echo "${ENTITLEMENT_KEY}" | docker login cp.icr.io --username cp --password-stdin
   ```

1. Pull the Vault Client image for your architecture:

   Architecture          | Image
   --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   amd64, arm64, ppc64le | `cp.icr.io/cp/ibm-vault-client/ibm-vault-client:<version>-ent.client`
   s390x                 | `cp.icr.io/cp/ibm-vault-client-for-z/ibm-vault-client-for-z:<version>-ent.client`

   For example:

   ```shell-session
   $ docker pull cp.icr.io/cp/ibm-vault-client/ibm-vault-client:2.2.2-ent.client
   ```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Step 2: Verify the installation

Run the `version` command and confirm that the output starts with
`Vault Client`.

<Tabs>

<Tab heading="Binary" group="binary">

```shell-session
$ vault-client version

Vault Client v2.2.2+ent ('<commit>'), built <date>
```

</Tab>

<Tab heading="Image archive" group="image-archive">

The container image entrypoint is `vault-client`, so pass the command as the container arguments:

```shell-session
$ docker run --rm hashicorp/vault-enterprise:2.2.2-ent.client version

Vault Client v2.2.2+ent ('<commit>'), built <date>
```

</Tab>

<Tab heading="IBM Entitled Registry" group="ier">

The container image entrypoint is `vault-client`, so pass the command as the container arguments:

```shell-session
$ docker run --rm cp.icr.io/cp/ibm-vault-client/ibm-vault-client:2.2.2-ent.client version

Vault Client v2.2.2+ent ('<commit>'), built <date>
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Next steps

- Run [Vault Agent](/vault/docs/agent-and-proxy/agent) with `vault-client agent`.
- Run [Vault Proxy](/vault/docs/agent-and-proxy/proxy) with `vault-client proxy`.
- Review the [CLI commands that Vault Client includes](/vault/docs/client#cli-commands).
